SRI SUDHEER G., PP  THIS CRIMINAL MISC. CASE HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 08.10.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY PASSED THE FOLLOWING:
 2025:KER:74340 Crl.M.C.No.10915/2024       3  ORDER
The petitioners are the accused Nos.1 and 2 in C.C.No.169/2024 on the files of the Chief Judicial Magistrate Court, Manjeri.
The offences alleged against them are under Sections 498A and 406 r/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
The second petitioner is the mother of the first petitioner.

2. The prosecution case is that the first petitioner, who married the defacto complainant on 12.06.2011, has been treating the defacto complainant with cruelty with the assistance of the second petitioner.
The case has been registered by the Areacode Police, Malappuram District on 07.01.2024, on the basis of the First Information Statement given by the defacto complainant.

3. After the completion of the investigation, the Sub Inspector of Police, Areacode Police Station,
laid the Final Report alleging the commission of the aforesaid offences.
4. In the present petition, the petitioners would contend that they are totally innocent, and that they have been falsely implicated in this case.
It is further contended that, none of the offences as alleged by the prosecution are attracted in the facts and circumstances of the case.
There is also a challenge that the prosecution initiated against the petitioners is barred by limitation.
5. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned Public Prosecutor representing the State of Kerala.

sentences.text: As already stated above, the case has been registered by the Areacode Police, on the basis of the First Information Statement given by the defacto complainant.
The copy of the aforesaid statement is produced as Annexure 1.
It is clear from Annexure 1 statement that the petitioner was subjected to severe physical and mental torture at the instance of the first petitioner.
The second petitioner is also alleged to have subjected her to very serious mental cruelty.

It is alleged by the defacto complainant that on one occasion, she was confined to a room, and was subjected to some rituals by the petitioners alleging that some evil spirit has been there in her body.
There is also the allegation that 20 sovereigns of gold ornaments which belonged to the defacto complainant was misappropriated by the petitioners.
7. As against the first petitioner, it is alleged that he even denied the paternity of the second child born in the wedlock with the defacto complainant.

The defacto complainant has also stated in the First Information Statement that on one occasion, she was taken to Thiruvananthapuram under the pretext of compromise talks, and was subjected to severe physical torture.
Thereafter, the defacto complainant is 2025:KER:74340       5 said to have taken shelter in her parental home and resided there.

8. The statement given by the defacto complainant in the above regard clearly brings home the necessary requirements of Section 498A IPC with regard to the physical and mental cruelty meted out by the petitioners.

9. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the First Information Statement in this case was given on 07.01.2024, and hence there is apparent bar of limitation in taking cognizance of the offences alleged against the petitioners.

10. I am not inclined to accept the above argument of the learned counsel for the petitioner, since it is apparent that the consequences of the physical and mental cruelty meted out to the defacto complainant is continuing even at the time when she lodged the First Information Statement before the Police.

It is stated by the defacto complainant in the concluding portion of her statement to the Investigating Officer that during the time when she was with her parents at her residence, neither the first petitioner nor his relatives contacted her, and took her back to their residence.
It is also alleged that the defacto complainant and her children were denied maintenance by the first petitioner throughout the aforesaid period.

11. Since it is clear from the above facts and circumstances of the 2025:KER:74340       6 case that the sufferings of mental and physical tortures meted out to the defacto complainant were continuing, it cannot be said that there is bar of limitation as far as this case is concerned.
12. It is true that the petitioners have taken a contention that false allegations are raised by the defacto complainant to implicate them in this criminal prosecution.
All those aspects are to be raised before the Trial Court at the appropriate stage of trial.

13. The learned counsel for the petitioner adverted to the complaint/Annexure 4, which the defacto complainant preferred before the Women's Commission in which she had stated about 50 sovereigns of gold ornaments which she was having at the time of her marriage.

It is pointed out by the learned counsel for the petitioner that as per the FI statement, the quantity of gold ornaments is Muhammed Babu vs State Of Kerala on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170921359/
3 mentioned as 20 sovereigns.

sentences.text: According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the above discrepancies itself show the falsity of the case projected by the defacto complainant.
14. I am not inclined to accept the above argument to invoke the exceptional powers of this Court under Section 528 BNSS and to quash the prosecution proceedings in this case.

Any variation in the quantity of gold ornaments mentioned by the defacto complainant in the above regard can only be considered as a trivial defect, which will not vitiate the prosecution 2025:KER:74340       7 proceedings in its entirety.
Having regard to the facts and circumstances of this case, I am of the view that there are absolutely no grounds to invoke the inherent powers of this Court to quash the prosecution proceedings.
Resultantly, the petition is hereby dismissed.
sd/ G.GIRISH JUDGE jm/
